purpose: Proposed claim-level academic records for question review. A future source-ledger release must formally adopt reviewed records before production use.

sources.title: Kant’s Moral Philosophy
sources.claim: The universal-law and humanity formulations have distinct roles; generic constraints alone do not establish Kantian ethics.

sources.title: Stoicism
sources.claim: The Stoic thesis that virtue alone is good differs from generic character valuation and emotional restraint.

sources.title: Dualism
sources.claim: Mind-body dualist views affirm mental and physical reality while denying their assimilation; an explanatory gap alone is insufficient.

sources.title: Libertarianism
sources.claim: Self-ownership and original claims over natural resources are distinct; right and left libertarian resource principles differ.

sources.title: Socialism
sources.claim: Effective worker or social control of productive assets distinguishes socialist families from redistribution alone; markets are not automatically excluded.

sources.title: Environmental Ethics
sources.claim: Ecological wholes can be proposed as bearers of value or standing independently of human or individual-animal welfare.

sources.title: Foundationalist Theories of Epistemic Justification
sources.claim: Foundationalism addresses the regress of justification through basic beliefs, not merely the possibility of one noninferentially justified belief.

sources.title: Feminist Bioethics
sources.claim: Relational accounts can treat social relations as constitutive of persons or autonomy rather than only causally influential.

sources.title: God and Other Ultimates
sources.claim: Personal and impersonal models of divine reality differ; a conditional characterization does not affirm existence.

sources.title: Miracles
sources.claim: Divine intervention is a proposed cause in some miracle concepts; mere possibility of a miracle is not an affirmation that a deity intervenes.

sources.title: Anarchism
sources.claim: Philosophical obligation skepticism and proposals for stateless political or legal institutions are distinct anarchist strands.
